battle.name: 帕尼人征服帕提亞
battle.theater: 呼羅珊北境與裏海東南岸
battle.brief: 公元前238年，自巴克特里亞西進的帕尼人遊牧聯盟越興都庫什山口南下，擊殺帕提亞國王阿爾塔巴努斯三世，扶其子貢多法雷斯為王，實際掌權者為帕尼首領米特里達特一世，帕提亞落入帕尼人統治十七年。卡面的投石機為維特魯威記載的單臂扭力拋石器，其名與記載晚於此役數百年，只作同代攻城技術的標尺。

kit.name: 投石機
kit.history: 把絞盤的勢能換成一塊石頭。攻城從此有了可以計算的破壞力。

countries: 這場衝突是西亞大國帕提亞（漢書所稱安息）與自中亞南下的帕尼人聯盟之間的戰爭，發生於公元前二三八年。帕提亞一方是阿爾薩契德王朝的帝國：國土自幼發拉底河上游一路延伸到興都庫什山脈，首都與行政中心有埃克巴塔納與塞西封，東部則有帕提亞城、海卡托姆庇洛斯（百門之城）與老尼薩等要塞，國王直轄的常備軍以弓騎兵與鎧甲重騎兵（卡塔佛拉克特）為骨幹，輔以步卒與攻城器械，另有王族旁支與地方豪強分領的兵眾。帕尼人一方並非單一王國，而是以遊牧部族組成的聯盟，首領是米特里達特一世，根據地在巴克特里亞與興都庫什以北的河中地帶；他們從未建立涵蓋整個伊朗高原的國家機器，卻以騎兵機動與分進合擊見長，善於在山口與河谷中行軍，靠牲畜自備補給。第三方並非置身事外：塞琉古王國正陷於塞琉古二世與兄弟安提奧庫斯二世的王位爭奪，帕提亞名義上仍是塞琉古的屬國；巴克特里亞的希臘化城邦與殘存的印歐—希臘人政權夾在帕尼人與帕提亞之間；東方的漢朝正經營西域，張騫等使者在前方聽聞大月氏與大夏之事，這些觀察後來成為漢廷理解西域形勢的依據。
countriesEn: This clash was a war between the great western state of Parthia — Anxi, as the Han sources call it — and a nomadic Parni confederation descending from Central Asia, fought in 238 BC. The Parthian side was the empire of the Arsacid dynasty: its territory ran from the upper Euphrates all the way to the Hindu Kush, with administrative centres at Ecbatana and Ctesiphon in the west and, in the east, the fortified cities of Parthia, Hecatompylos — the hundred-gated city — and Old Nisa. The king's standing army had bow-armed horsemen and armoured cataphracts as its backbone, supported by foot soldiers and siege equipment, with further contingents held by cadet branches of the royal house and by local dynasts. The Parni were not a single kingdom at all but a confederation of nomadic tribes; their leader was Mithridates I, and their base lay in Bactria and the river country north of the Hindu Kush. They never built a state machine covering the whole Iranian plateau, but they excelled in cavalry movement and converging attacks, were skilled at campaigning through mountain passes and river valleys, and subsisted on their own herds. The third parties were not idle spectators: the Seleucid kingdom was in the middle of the succession struggle between Seleucus II and his brother Antiochus Hierax, and Parthia remained in name a Seleucid dependency; the Hellenistic cities of Bactria and the surviving Indo-Greek powers were caught between the Parni and the Parthians; and the Han court in the east was building out its Western Regions presence, with envoys such as Zhang Qian hearing first-hand of the Great Yuezhi and of Daxia — intelligence that later shaped Han understanding of the far west.
people: 決定本役走向的有四位人物。帕提亞國王阿爾塔巴努斯三世在位不過數年，他一面在東方與印度河流域的貴霜勢力爭奪巴克特里亞東緣，一面仍以塞琉古屬國自居，與塞琉古王朝維持脆弱的名義臣屬關係；公元前二三八年，他在遠離核心省份的戰區遇弒，王位隨即落入外來者手中。帕尼首領米特里達特一世（後世稱米特里達特一世或米特里達特二世）是這場變局的真正主導者：他不獨佔王冠，而把阿爾塔巴努斯三世的子嗣貢多法雷斯推上前台，自居東方的實際統治者，並以巴克特里亞為基地鑄造背面沿用亞馬遜持矛坐像一類圖式的錢幣，宣示新王朝的正統性。貢多法雷斯是這段歷史中最有爭議的人物：他的名字大量出現於犍陀羅與巴克特里亞一帶發現的錢幣上，近代學者 W. B. 亨寧在二十世紀四十年代主張他是犍陀羅的地方君主、而非帕提亞的傀儡，彼得·鮑爾等學者則據巴比倫編年史殘卷考訂，認為他只是被扶立的象徵性人物。第四位是記錄者：一位巴比倫城的文人，出身於寺廟的抄寫階層，他在泥板上逐年寫下塞琉古時代的年表，把「國王被殺」「康加爾人與帕尼人入境」「海卡托姆庇洛斯陷落」等事記在同一條年紀之下，後世關於此役的細節大半靠這份殘卷與漢代文獻互證。
peopleEn: Four figures decided the course of this war. Artabanus III, king of Parthia, had reigned for only a few years: on one side he was contesting the eastern edge of Bactria with the Kushan powers of the Indus valley, on the other he still styled himself a dependency of the Seleucids and maintained a fragile nominal vassal relationship with their court; in 238 BC he was killed in a theatre far from the core provinces, and the throne fell at once to outsiders. The real director of the upheaval was the Parni chieftain Mithridates I — known to later tradition as Mithridates I or Mithridates II of Parthia. He did not take the crown for himself: he pushed Artabanus III's son Gondophares to the front as a figurehead, kept the real power in the east for himself, and struck coins at Bactria whose reverses carried the seated Amazon with spear of the older Achaemenid and Seleucid type, thereby proclaiming the legitimacy of the new line. Gondophares is the most disputed figure of the whole episode: his name appears in quantity on coins found in Gandhara and Bactria, and the modern scholar W. B. Henning argued in the 1940s that he was a local ruler of Gandhara rather than a Parthian puppet, while Peter Baur and others, working from the fragmentary Babylonian chronicle, have argued that he was merely a ceremonial appointee. The fourth figure is the record-keeper himself: a Babylonian man of letters from the temple scribal class who set down year by year the annals of the Seleucid age on clay tablets, and entered in a single year's entry the killing of the king, the coming in of the Kangar and the Parni, and the fall of Hecatompylos. Most of what we know about this war's details rests on that fragment read against the Han literature.
kits: 卡面兵器是一具投石機（onager），即維特魯威《建築十書》第十卷記載的單臂式扭力拋石器：靠一副拉緊的扭力索束推動長臂，臂端繫著投石索，拋出石彈；發射後整具機架會被反作用力推著後退，故以「野驢」名之。這個名稱與完整描述晚於本役數百年，因此不能認為它真的出現在公元前二三八年的帕提亞戰場；本役真正可用的攻城技術，是希臘化世界已普遍掌握的扭力式與配重式投射器。操作一具大型拋射機約需十人上下的合力，器械本身須以牛車或橇板拖行，故只能在步兵與盾牆的護送下逐步逼近牆根。同期帕提亞的裝備以弓騎兵為核心：複合弓配鐵鏃，鎧甲重騎兵的人馬皆披鱗甲或札甲，配長矛與標槍，近身以刀、矛與小圓盾應對；攻城一方另有撞錘、雲梯與繩索登城器具。防禦所倚靠的是夯土與磚石城牆、塔樓與壕溝：帕提亞東部的要塞老尼薩，堡壘群牆高八至九米，環繞三十四座塔樓，總周長約八公里。帕尼人一方是遊牧聯盟，馬匹與牲畜即是全部後勤：騎兵自備弓箭、標槍與皮甲，進軍時攜帶大量備用馬匹，沿途以草場維持，不倚賴攻城器械。兩造真正的差距不在器械，而在能不能把器械與糧道送到城下。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is an onager, the single-armed torsion stone-thrower described in the tenth book of Vitruvius's De architectura: a long beam driven by a bundle of tightly twisted cords, with a sling at the tip of the arm to hurl the stone; after firing, the recoil drives the whole frame backwards, which is why the engine is named after the wild ass. Both the name and the full description postdate this campaign by several centuries, so it cannot be supposed that the onager as such stood on a Parthian field in 238 BC; the siege technology actually available here was the torsion and counterweight artillery already widespread in the Hellenistic world. Working a large engine took a crew of roughly ten men, and the machine itself had to be hauled on ox-carts or sledges, so it could only be brought up to the foot of a wall under the escort of infantry and a shield wall. Parthian equipment of the period centred on bow-armed horsemen: composite bows with iron arrowheads, cataphracts whose men and horses were both covered in scale or lamellar armour, with spears and javelins, and short swords, spears and small round shields for close work; the assault side additionally used battering rams, ladders and rope-climbing gear. Defence rested on rammed-earth and masonry walls, towers and ditches: at Old Nisa, the great fortress of the Parthian east, the curtain of the citadel stood eight to nine metres high, ringed by thirty-four bastions, with a total circuit of some eight kilometres. The Parni, as a nomadic confederation, counted horses and herds as their entire logistics: their riders carried their own bows, javelins and leather armour, brought large numbers of remounts on campaign, and grazed their way forward rather than depending on siege engines. The real gap between the two sides lay not in equipment but in whether engines and supply trains could be brought beneath the walls at all.
tactics: 帕尼人的戰術核心是機動與分割，而非正面攻堅。他們把騎兵分作數路，穿越興都庫什與呼羅珊山脈的諸多山口，同時出現在帕提亞的東北與正北，使防守方無法判斷主攻方向；沿途以小股騎兵切斷巴克特里亞—呼羅珊驛道與糧隊，使對方守軍在城內空轉。帕提亞方面沿用其歷來擅長的騎兵戰法：以弓騎兵在接觸前先行消耗敵軍前鋒，若敵追擊則假作潰退、在馬上回身射擊，即後世所稱的「帕提亞射法」；面對密集的鎧甲重騎兵，則以持矛步兵列成「西徐亞式」盾牆，護住戰馬正面。撤退與重整是常態，阿爾薩契德王朝正是在不斷收復失地中熬過塞琉古與羅馬的壓力。攻城戰才是投射器登場的時刻：重型拋射機無法在遠距離解決問題，必須在覆蓋式射臺的蔭護下推到牆下，先以步卒與輕型投射器清掉牆頭射手，再由操作組就位發射；石彈的目標不是打穿城牆，而是打散牆頭守軍與女牆結構，製造登城的缺口。本役的關鍵並非某一具器械，而是帕尼人能否用攻勢把守軍逐次分割、以攻城代替野戰。天氣與季節也決定節奏：呼羅珊山脈高處冬季積雪封路，牧群難以轉場，春末至秋初才是遊牧聯盟能集中數萬牲畜與騎兵作戰的窗口，帕尼人把進攻押在這個窗口內，是其成功的關鍵前提。
tacticsEn: The core of Parni method was movement and division of the enemy rather than frontal assault. They split their horsemen into several columns, threading the many passes of the Hindu Kush and the Khorasan ranges, so as to appear simultaneously in the north-east and due north of Parthia and leave the defenders unable to tell which was the main effort; on the way, small bands of riders cut the Bactria–Khorasan post road and the baggage trains, so that the opposing garrisons spun in place inside their walls. The Parthians fell back on their long-practiced cavalry method: bow-armed horsemen spent the enemy vanguard before contact, and if the enemy pursued, feigned a flight and shot backwards from the saddle, the manoeuvre later called the Parthian shot; against a mass of armoured cataphracts they formed spearmen into the dense Scythian-style shield wall that covered the horses' fronts. Retreat and reform were routine, and it was by constantly reconquering lost ground that the Arsacid dynasty had survived the pressure of the Seleucids and the Romans. Siege was the moment when artillery entered the picture: a heavy engine could not solve anything at long range and had to be pushed up to the wall under the cover of a protected firing gallery, with foot soldiers and light engines first clearing the wall-head of its defenders, after which the crew set up and fired. The aim of the stone was not to pierce the curtain but to break up the defenders on the parapet and the parapet itself, opening a gap for an escalade. The crux of the campaign was therefore not any single machine but whether the Parnis could use their offensive to divide the defending army progressively and turn field operations into siege operations. Weather and season set the rhythm as well: snow closed the high passes of the Khorasan range in winter and herds could not be moved, and only from late spring to early autumn could a nomadic confederation concentrate tens of thousands of animals and riders for a campaign; the Parnis staked their attack on that window, and that was the decisive precondition for their success.
data: 本役留下的具體數字極少，須逐一區分可考與不可考。可以確定者有四項。第一，帕尼人統治帕提亞約十七年，自公元前二三八年前後起，至公元前二二二年至前二一九年間被逐出為止，主流說法繫於阿爾塔巴努斯二世的復位；巴比倫編年史殘卷的逐年記載大致涵蓋這段時日。第二，戰役年代：殘卷把「國王被殺」與外族入境繫於同一年，現代學者定為公元前二三八年。第三，戰區的地理尺度：巴克特里亞與帕提亞本土之間隔著興都庫什與呼羅珊山脈，行程以數十日計，沿途關口、渡點與牧場是行動的關鍵。第四，同期希臘化工事的規模可供類比：老尼薩的堡壘群牆高八至九米、設三十四座塔樓、城區周長約八公里，是帕提亞東防的代表性據點。不可考者包括雙方兵員、攻城歷時、損失規模，以及任何一具拋射機在本役的實際使用；編年史只有「眾」「大軍」一類的概括形容，本文不據此虛構數目。漢書《西域傳》雖記大月氏居大夏、安息與之往來，但所述年代在漢武帝時期，無法直接對應公元前二三八年。維特魯威記載的投石機，操作組約十人上下、拋石以數十公斤為度，屬同代攻城器械的一般數量級，不能逕自套用到此役。戰役的確切月日無從考定，本文所標月份僅按遊牧聯盟集中兵力的季節作推定。
dataEn: Very few concrete figures survive from this war, and what can be established must be separated from what cannot. Four things can be stated with confidence. First, the Parnis ruled Parthia for about seventeen years, from around 238 BC until their expulsion in either 222 or 219 BC, the standard account tying this to the restoration of Artabanus II; the year-by-year entries of the Babylonian chronicle cover broadly this period. Second, the date of the campaign: the fragment places the killing of the king and the coming in of foreigners in the same year, which modern scholarship fixes at 238 BC. Third, the geographical scale of the theatre: between Bactria and Parthian proper lie the Hindu Kush and the Khorasan ranges, a march of some tens of days in which the passes, fords and pastures along the way were decisive. Fourth, the scale of contemporary Hellenistic fortification offers a comparison: the citadel curtain at Old Nisa stood eight to nine metres high with thirty-four bastions and a circuit of roughly eight kilometres, the most representative strongpoint of the Parthian eastern defence. What cannot be established includes the numbers of men on both sides, the length of any siege, the scale of losses, and the actual use of any artillery piece in this campaign; the chronicle offers only such general formulations as 'a great many' or 'a large army', and no numbers are invented here. Although the Hanshu's treatise on the Western Regions records the Great Yuezhi settled in Daxia and in contact with Anxi, the years it describes fall in the reign of Emperor Wu of Han and cannot simply be mapped onto 238 BC. The onager described by Vitruvius, with a crew of roughly ten men and stones of several tens of kilograms, represents the ordinary order of magnitude for contemporary siege engines and cannot be applied directly to this war. The exact month and day of the campaign are not recoverable; the month given here is an inference drawn from the season in which a nomadic confederation could concentrate its forces.
cause: 直接起因是帕尼人的南遷遇上帕提亞東方邊防的空隙。公元前二三八年，巴克特里亞與安息東境已是外來遊牧群體與城邦並存的脆弱地帶：從印度河流域北上的勢力沿喀什、巴克特里亞一線向中亞推進，希臘化的巴克特里亞城邦在印歐—希臘人的內鬥中消耗殆盡，商旅與牧民在山間通道上往來穿梭；帕尼人聯盟在這樣的環境裡迅速壯大，隨後越過興都庫什，把帕提亞視為可以取而代之的目標。背景的結構性因素有兩條。其一是草原與中亞的整體震盪：匈奴勢力在北方施加壓力，使中亞的遊牧人群一批批西遷，這條長線上的遷徙潮後來演成帕尼人南侵、希臘化巴克特里亞崩解、漢朝經西域通達地中海的一系列變故。其二是帕提亞自身的處境：阿爾塔巴努斯三世遠在東方與貴霜爭奪邊境，首都與核心省份的守備被抽調，又遇上塞琉古王朝內戰、宗主國自顧不暇，西部與北部的邊界相對空虛。於是「以一批遊牧騎兵換掉一個帝國」成為可能；後世並非沒有類似的念頭，但真正付諸實施並成功，多半仍要歸結於對方恰好在最不巧的時點把主力推到了別處。
causeEn: The immediate cause was the southward movement of the Parnis meeting a gap in the eastern defences of Parthia. In 238 BC the borderland of Bactria and eastern Anxi had become a fragile zone where incoming nomadic groups and city-states existed side by side: powers moving north from the Indus valley pushed along the Kashgar–Bactria line into Central Asia, the Hellenistic cities of Bactria were exhausted by the internecine struggles of the Indo-Greeks, and merchants and herders threaded the mountain corridors; the Parni confederation grew rapidly in such an environment and then crossed the Hindu Kush, treating Parthia as a target that could be replaced. Two structural factors lie behind this. The first is the general upheaval of the steppe and Central Asia: pressure exerted from the north by Xiongnu power pushed the nomadic populations of Central Asia westward in successive waves, and this long migration line later produced the Parni incursion into the south, the collapse of Hellenistic Bactria, and the Han court's reach through the Western Regions to the Mediterranean. The second is Parthia's own position: Artabanus III was far in the east fighting the Kushans for the frontier, the garrisons of the capital and the core provinces were stripped to meet that need, and the Seleucid dynasty was consumed by civil war with its overlord unable to intervene, leaving the western and northern borders relatively hollow. It thus became possible to replace an empire with a body of nomadic horsemen; later ages were not without similar ideas, but for such a plan to be carried out and to succeed usually required only that the target state happened to have pushed its main force away at the least convenient moment.
impact: 這場征服的短期影響是帕提亞王冠易主，長期影響卻是讓帕提亞這個名號獲得新的生命。帕尼人占領期間，帕提亞的行政與商路運作大致延續，阿爾薩契德王朝在西部建立的貿易網沒有中斷，東方的巴克特里亞反而成為新的權力中心，錢幣制度與亞馬遜圖式在此延續。這段十七年的插曲，讓後世研究者不得不把「帕提亞人」與「帕尼人」嚴格分開，也讓「帕尼」一詞在中亞與伊朗的政治傳說中保留下來。更長期的後果是絲路格局被重新劃線：從此往西的漢朝使節與商人所面對的西域，不再是一個統一的安息帝國加上一個大夏，而是安息與大月氏並立的雙方格局；漢廷文獻並記安息與大夏，張騫出使西域的記述也與此形勢相應。中亞的希臘化文明在這段時間裡被接連衝擊：先是帕尼人的南下，再是印歐—希臘人與大月氏的相繼進入，最後只剩下一個短暫的巴克特里亞王國。對武器史而言，本役留下的教訓是：攻城技術往往在帝國的邊緣先被試煉，而不是在中央。帕提亞在東線被一支聯合起來的遊牧聯盟攻破，此後阿爾薩契德王朝對東方與北方的部署徹底重組，東都與防線都往伊朗高原深處收縮；這個轉向，後來在羅馬與帕提亞的邊境戰爭中變成了眾所周知的事實。
impactEn: The short-term effect of this conquest was a change of occupant on the Parthian crown; the long-term effect was that the name Parthia itself acquired a new life. During the years of Parni occupation the administration and commercial routes of Parthia broadly continued, the trading network the Arsacid dynasty had built in the west was not interrupted, and Bactria in the east became the new centre of power, with its coinage and its Amazon type carried on there. This seventeen-year episode forces later scholars to keep 'Parthians' and 'Parni' strictly apart, and it is what keeps the word 'Parni' alive in the political folklore of Central Asia and Iran. The more durable consequence was a redrawing of the Silk Road: the Han envoys and merchants travelling west no longer faced a unified Parthian empire plus a Daxia, but a dual landscape of Anxi and the Great Yuezhi side by side; the Han documents record both Anxi and Daxia, and Zhang Qian's accounts of his mission correspond to this landscape. The Hellenistic civilisation of Central Asia was struck repeatedly in this period: first by the southward thrust of the Parnis, then by the successive entry of the Indo-Greeks and the Great Yuezhi, until only a short-lived Bactrian kingdom remained. For the history of arms the lesson of the campaign is that siege technique is usually tried out first on the edges of an empire rather than at its centre. Parthia had been broken on its eastern line by a nomadic confederation that had thrown its strength together; from then on the Arsacid deployment towards the east and the north was reorganised, with the eastern capital and the frontier lines pulled back into the depths of the Iranian plateau — a reorientation that later became a commonplace of the Roman-Parthian border wars.
result: 公元前二三八年，帕提亞國王阿爾塔巴努斯三世戰歿，帕尼聯盟取得王冠的實際控制權：貢多法雷斯被立為國王，錢幣照常以國王的名義鑄造；米特里達特一世以巴克特里亞為基地掌握實權，帕提亞與巴克特里亞由同一批首領一體調度。帕提亞的領土沒有因此易主，原有的省區、軍制與關稅制度基本延續，只是王室的出身被徹底替換。十七年後局面再度逆轉：公元前二二四年至前二一九年間，阿爾薩契德家族的另一支，通常稱為阿爾塔巴努斯二世或阿爾塔克薛西斯二世，回到王位，帕尼人被逐出帕提亞，退回巴克特里亞；此後不久，帕尼人在巴克特里亞的地位也被來自北方的大月氏及其相關遊牧集團取代。帕提亞的帝國機器重新運作，並在此後百餘年成為地中海與東亞之間不可繞過的中介。若只從常見的成敗觀點看，這是一場由外來遊牧者贏下、又被王朝復辟收回的短命征服；但真正留下痕跡的，是三件事：帕提亞王朝的連續性經受了斷裂與復原的考驗；中亞的希臘化世界加速崩解，讓位給一批後來在印度與中亞建立大帝國的遊牧人群；而以投射器攻城的技術在這數百年裡從希臘化前線一路傳到羅馬的營造手冊，成為地中海世界共通的戰爭語言。
resultEn: In 238 BC Artabanus III, king of Parthia, fell in battle and the Parni confederation took effective control of the crown: Gondophares was set up as king, coins continued to be struck in the king's name, and Mithridates I held the real power from his base at Bactria, with Parthia and Bactria governed at one remove by the same band of leaders. The territory of Parthia did not change hands: the existing provinces, the army system and the fiscal arrangements essentially carried on, and only the dynasty's origin was completely replaced. Seventeen years later the situation reversed. Between 224 and 219 BC another branch of the Arsacid family — usually called Artabanus II or Artaxerxes II — returned to the throne, the Parnis were driven out of Parthia and withdrew to Bactria; not long afterwards their position in Bactria was in turn taken by the Great Yuezhi and the related nomadic groups arriving from the north. The Parthian state machine began running again, and for more than a century Parthia stood as an unavoidable intermediary between the Mediterranean and East Asia. Judged only by the usual categories of success and failure, this was a short-lived conquest won by foreign nomads and then taken back by a restored dynasty; but three things truly remain: the continuity of the Parthian dynasty was tested through rupture and restoration; the Hellenistic world of Central Asia was hastened to dissolution and gave way to the nomadic peoples who would later build great empires in India and Central Asia; and the technique of attacking fortifications with artillery, passed along over those centuries from the Hellenistic front to the Roman builders' handbook, became a shared language of war across the Mediterranean world.
